messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. They want:

1. In New York: libraries with Reading Room and Fiction section.
2. In Los Angeles: libraries with Wi-Fi and Children Section.
3. In Chicago: libraries with Cafe and Reading Room.

We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with appropriate facilities. The function expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe". But the facilities parameter seems to accept only one value? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." It might accept an array? The type signature shows facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[], but the syntax is weird: "Cafe"[] maybe means array of "Cafe"? Actually it might mean facilities can be one of those strings or an array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. Possibly it's a mistake; maybe they intended facilities to be an array of strings from that set. Let's assume we can pass an array of strings.

Thus we need to call the function three times. We'll do separate calls. We'll produce JSON calls.
